source.title: Skill over Scale: The Case for Medium, Domain-Specific Models for SE

record.tranche_reason: The study compares downstream results across two SOBert sizes and reports that larger models do not consistently perform better; it also says downstream performance saturates while pretraining loss continues to decline. It does not directly test fitted language-model scaling laws.
record.gate_note: The study uses a cited scaling-law rule (about 20 times more training tokens than parameters) to help choose its training budget, but does not test that rule or a compute-optimal allocation. Its validation-loss plot and comparisons of downstream performance across model sizes bear on V1 and V6, respectively. Results cited from other work are not recorded.
record.test_reason: The study compares fine-tuned downstream F1 of two SOBert sizes (125M vs 762M) on four tasks. The authors argue against 'larger is better' for fine-tuned models, noting downstream saturation while pre-training loss keeps falling. This is a weak, two-point test bearing only on V6. The Figure 5 loss curves fit no power law and give no numbers, so V1 is not tested. The Chinchilla 20-tokens-per-parameter rule is used only to pick the training budget (V3 assumed, not tested).
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that carefully pre-trained, modestly sized in-domain models (SOBert) outperform general BERTs, GPT-3.5/4 and fine-tuned 7B Llamas on four StackOverflow labeling tasks. They also find no consistent trend of larger fine-tuned models beating smaller ones, which they attribute to fine-tuning. Downstream performance saturated around 50k steps while loss kept declining.
record.recipe_differences: The study trains BERT-style masked-language models on StackOverflow data and evaluates fine-tuned downstream tasks; it does not reproduce the original scaling-law fits or compute-optimal allocation experiments.
record.method_sensitivity: The authors report that downstream performance saturates around 50,000 pre-training steps for both SOBert models, although pre-training loss continues to decline.
record.peer_reviewed: 2025 IEEE/ACM Second International Conference on AI Foundation Models and Software Engineering (Forge)
record.problems: Only two SOBert sizes are compared, and the study does not fit scaling curves or report uncertainty for the downstream metrics. Validation-loss values are presented in a figure without extracted numeric values. The authors note that downstream performance saturates before pre-training loss does.

untested.parts: Power-law form, exponents, and scaling in parameters, data or compute over orders of magnitude. Only two loss curves over steps are plotted.
All parts. No extrapolation from small to large runs.
All parts. The 20-tokens-per-parameter rule is used as a design rationale only.
All parts. Shape is not varied at fixed parameter count.
All parts. Fine-tuning is used, but no power-law fit is made in that regime.
Smooth scaling curves across many sizes, and prediction from loss values. Only two sizes, about 6x apart, are compared, with no uncertainty reported.

missing.what: Pairwise comparisons of BERT-Base-uncased (110M) vs BERT-Large (340M), fine-tuned. F1: NER 0.55 vs 0.63; quality 0.82 vs 0.71; closed question 0.56 vs 0.43; obsoletion 0.70 vs 0.47. The larger model wins only on NER. The authors cite these in Sec. VI-B as part of the 'no consistent trend' argument.
missing.locator: Table I; Table II; Section VI-B

record.verdict_notes: The study's own text is inconsistent with its tables. Sec. VI-B says Base beat Large on closed question and obsoletion, while Table I shows NER Base > Large and closed question F1 tied. Sec. V says closed question is the second task after NER where Large is outperformed. Verdicts follow the table numbers. The V6 evidence is weak: two sizes, fine-tuning on top, no error bars, and small test sets (obsoletion has 942 samples). GPT-3.5 vs GPT-4 is not a controlled scale comparison and was not used.

versions.untested_parts: Only validation-loss curves for SOBertBase and SOBertLarge are shown. The study does not fit or test power-law form, estimate exponents, test parameter- or compute-scaling, or establish behavior over several orders of magnitude.
No prediction from smaller runs to substantially larger runs is evaluated.
The compute-optimal parameter/token split is cited as a design rationale, not tested.
Depth and width are not varied at fixed parameter count.
No other modalities or training regimes are tested.
Downstream results are compared for two SOBert sizes on four StackOverflow tasks; the study does not test broad downstream scaling curves or general prediction from pretraining loss.
The study does not compare fitted exponents, fitting choices, or compute-optimal allocations.
